Mohn.et: With widespread dialectal -ā- → -ō- (as also in ohne and wo) from obsolete Mahn, from Middle High German māhe, māhen (Central German also already mān), from Old High German māho, from Proto-West Germanic *māhō, from Proto-Germanic *mēhô. Compare the variant Ol…

Möhre.et: From Middle High German morhe, morche, from Old High German morha, from Proto-West Germanic *morhā, from Proto-Germanic *murhǭ. Cognate with obsolete English more (“carrot, parsnip”).

s: „So wie sich ein Mohr nicht weiß waschen läßt, so läßt sich auch mancher Thor nicht klug machen.“
"Just as a Moor cannot be washed white, so can many a fool also not be made wise."
Mohr.et: From Middle High German mōr, mōre, Old High German Mōr, from Latin Maurus, 8th c.

s: Friedrich Mohs, German mineralogist, the originator of Mohs scale of mineral hardness.

Mohar.et: Borrowed from Hungarian mohár and Czech mohár, from Serbo-Croatian mòhār.
